kept.spine: Market day is Rundgate at its plainest. The stalls fill because the road brings the trade to them.
Armed order is part of Rundgate's furniture, and the town pays professionals for its safety rather than trusting to luck.
People here can afford to argue about things other than money.
The town expects to carry on much as it has.
Rundgate is defended properly rather than impressively, and none of its works are for show.
Children here are taught the rules about the dark early, and the rules work.
The watch answers what is reported to it and does not go looking for more.
Prices stay steady here, in a way that suggests the town is not living on the last thing it sold.
The town has somebody who can do what is usually needed and knows what lies beyond that.
The town sits on the way to somewhere else, and has made a modest living from being passed through.
The road brings in what the town cannot grow for itself.
The city is large enough to have quarters that scarcely know each other.
The town has had pressure enough to bend its relationships, and they have not bent. They stand no different than they would anywhere else.
